To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the developing rat liver, chondroitan sulfate synthesis is elevated two- to three-fold during fetal development and decreases to adult levels within the first two weeks of life, while the synthesis of hepran sulfate is almost unaltered.

the synthesis of chondoitin sulfate is elevated in fetal liver tissue as compared with the neonatal and adult counterpart, which is due to the elevated activity of the UDP-xylose:core-protein xylosyltransferases.

the developmentally regulated changes in proteoglycan composition in rat liver are due to a postnatal down regulation of chondroitan sulfate synthesis in hepatocytes and that the synthesis of both heparin sulfate and chondroin sulfate is dependent upon protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a developmental change from chondroitin to heparan sulfate as the main proteoglycan synthesized in rat liver during postnatal development and the identification of hepatocytes as the cell type which is mainly responsible for elevated chondoitin sulfate production in embryonic liver tissue.

a detailed characterization of the developmental pattern of sulfated proteochondroitin synthesis in rat liver tissue and isolated hepatocytes and the elucidation of its cellular and biochemical basis.
the identification of the cell type and the molecular mechanism of elevated chondroitian sulfate production in developing rat liver.

in fetal liver the synthesis of chondoitin sulfate is enhanced two to three times as compared with the synthesis of hepran sulfate and that this synthesis is shut down rapidly after birth.

the development of liver proteoglycane formation is characterized by a postnatal shut down and a subsequent reactivation of chondroitinsulfate synthesis in liver cells, whereas heparan sulfate synthesis remains unchanged.
the synthesis of sulfated glycosamino glycans is developmentally regulated.

the synthesis of sulfated glycosamino- glycans in the liver is subject to developmental regulation and that chondroitin sulfates play an essential role in the development of liver tissue.
the synthesis of sulfated glycosamino- and proteoglyc can is regulated during development of rat liver.
